content.content:
The detail panel presents every id listed in its four relationship sections — "depends_on", "evaluates", "dependents" and "evaluators" (rmovtvkt) — as a visible link rather than as bare text. The entry reads as a link: it is drawn so that a reader can see it is something to follow, set apart from the plain text of the section around it, instead of standing as a run of characters that merely happens to be an id. Being visible is the whole of the commitment: the entry's own appearance says that the id is followable, rather than leaving the reader to find that out by trying.

The entry's text is unchanged, and it is the whole of the link's text: the link shows the bare id — the same characters the selected node's field holds — with no label, no node summary, no quoted title, no icon or "go to" control beside it, no shortening and no reformatting. The section therefore keeps reporting the edges the node records in the ids that record uses (rmovtvkt), so the panel and the field cannot disagree about which node is named, and this decision adds no element to the section: only the look of the entry that is already there.

This is a decision about appearance and nothing else. What the four sections list is rmovtvkt's, down to a section with no entries appearing with its label and its explicit empty state; what activating a listed entry does is kwxutvpw's, one selection and one detail render, by pointer click or by Enter or Space while the entry has focus. The link is the look of an entry that was already activatable. It is not a second activation, not an extra input and not a change to what any input does, so nothing here restates or narrows the activation kwxutvpw settled, and nothing here makes an entry activatable that was not.

The link belongs to the ids listed inside those four sections and to nothing else in the panel. An id the panel mentions anywhere else — inside the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, on the canvas, or in a section's empty state — is not an entry in a relationship section and gains nothing from this decision. All four sections are covered alike, and a listed id is presented this way whether it names a decision or an evaluation (zkvxornu, kwxutvpw), because an evaluation's id is an entry that selects its node exactly as a decision's does.

The look stops at being a link. This decision does not say which colour role the entry takes, whether a pointer cursor is shown over it, what happens to the entry on hover, what marks it while it has focus, which element carries the look, or which class vocabulary names it: each of those is a separate commitment with its own check, and none of them is fixed, required, forbidden or implied here. Nor does this decision add any class, style property or stylesheet rule itself. It states that the entry is presented as a link; the parts of that presentation are settled where they are owned.

One case stays where rusopkql put it: an id that names no node document. That entry stays listed among its siblings in its section and stays inert when activated (rusopkql), and its look is not settled here. The decisions that own that case may present it as an entry like its siblings, or present it muted and without the link cue; neither is forbidden by this decision, which commits a listed entry to not reading as bare text and leaves the presentation of the entry that cannot be followed to its own decision. Nothing here narrows the entry, drops it, or changes what activating it does, and nothing here requires the entry that names a node and the entry that names none to look alike.
content.rationale:
kwxutvpw made every listed id an activatable entry and then deliberately left the entry's appearance alone, so as things stand the panel holds a control whose look says nothing about it: an entry that can be followed to the node it names reads exactly like the prose beside it, and a reader who arrives in the panel already holding an id has to try an id-shaped string on the chance that it responds. The affordance is the missing half of an activation that exists, and a link look is its smallest form — no element, no text, no behaviour, only the entry's own appearance carrying the fact that the id can be followed. That is also why this decision is the right place to stop: it fills exactly what kwxutvpw left unstated and decides none of what kwxutvpw settled, so activation keeps its one outcome and its inputs, and the sections keep their contents and their frames.

The link's text stays the bare id because the section's job is to report what the selected node's fields record (rmovtvkt), and because an id is the only name a reader can carry to the canvas or to another section and be sure of arriving at the same node. A label, a node summary or a shortened id would put the panel's rendering of the node where the graph's own record belongs, and would leave the reader comparing a prettified entry against the id the field holds. Keeping the text and adding only the look keeps one account of the id across the field, the section and the activation, which is what lets a reader trust the entry to name what the section says it names.

Stopping at the existence of the look is what lets the rest be decided at all. The colour role the entry takes, the pointer cursor, the hover rule, the focus outline and the class vocabulary are stylesheet facts a reviewer can point at in the styles, so each is checkable on its own terms and belongs to the decision that owns it; settled here, they would either be restated by those decisions or contradicted by them, and the distinction between an entry that reads as a link and whatever draws the link would be lost. The same restraint keeps rusopkql's case open: that decision kept an id naming no node listed and inert while leaving the entry's appearance to the presentation decisions, and an entry that names nothing can honestly be presented as the different case it is — muted, cue-free — only if this decision commits the link look for a listed entry and leaves the look of the entry that names nothing to be decided as the different case it is, rather than fixing one look for every listed id alike.
